aidb_assessment.novelty: High conceptual novelty within the supplied paper: it separates residency from retrievability inside a KV-evicting multi-turn server and treats rotary distance as a second controlled cache objective. The engineering combination of planner foresight, bounded exact re-rotation, persistence, and non-compounding reference keys is also distinctive.
aidb_assessment.rationale: The controlled Qwen3-8B comparisons, fresh-seed headline run, distance intervention, factorial ablations, integrity protocol, and very-long-session results make the central finding credible enough to influence evaluation design. Adoption is premature because external validity is narrow, planner robustness is under-characterized, the second-model component comparison is inconclusive, concurrency is untested, and executable artifacts are not supplied here.
aidb_assessment.usefulness: Potentially high for planned coding and tool agents under strict accelerator-memory budgets. The strongest immediate value is diagnostic: cache evaluations should measure both needed-token residency and physical positional distance. Production usefulness remains contingent on realistic planner errors, diverse workloads, concurrent serving, and temporal-semantics tests.

executive_summary: PACE addresses two distinct failures in budgeted KV caches: needed tokens can be evicted, or retained yet difficult to use because their rotary-position distance is large. It combines planner-directed retention with exact, bounded-position renumbering. Controlled Qwen3-8B results are strong: PACE substantially outperforms standard eviction and either component alone, and retains quality through very long synthetic coding sessions. The mechanism evidence is persuasive but narrow: one synthetic task family, mostly oracle plans, two small models, one GPU type, small cells, and no matched full-cache control at the headline length. The paper is valuable and merits replication before production adoption, especially under noisy plans, realistic workloads, concurrency, and time-sensitive tasks where collapsed gaps may alter semantics.

assumptions: The planner can identify which earlier spans later steps will need.
The protected spans generally fit the token budget; otherwise restoration or prioritization is required.
Collapsing positional gaps preserves the semantics relevant to the evaluated task.
A fixed foresight bonus remains above the cumulative-attention scores of unprotected tokens over the tested session lengths.
The synthetic coding benchmark’s dependency and recall structure is informative about broader planned-agent workloads.
key_components: Plan-aware retention converts a dependency blueprint into span-level future references and adds a dominant bonus to cumulative-attention scores.
Bounded positions collapse gaps left by eviction, preserve retained-token order, and exactly re-rotate cached keys to their new physical positions.
Persistent sessions append only new messages and preserve cache state and prior eviction decisions across agent steps.
Tiered rehydration restores planner-requested spans from host memory, local storage, or a remote cache.
A reference store derives later key positions from a stable copy to prevent repeated bf16 rounding from accumulating.
method.overview: PACE modifies an inference engine’s KV-cache manager. A planner supplies dependencies over earlier message spans; a foresight bonus makes future-referenced spans outrank unreferenced tokens, prioritizing the soonest use. Separately, retained tokens are periodically renumbered in logical order and cached keys are re-rotated so their physical positions remain bounded. Persistent sessions carry eviction state between turns, while optional memory tiers can restore planned spans that were evicted. A reference-key store prevents rounding error from compounding across repeated renumbering.

open_questions: Does bounded-position renumbering improve real repository-scale coding, tool-use, research, and multi-agent workflows when dependencies and distractors arise naturally?
What planner precision and recall thresholds preserve an advantage over retention-only and retrieval-based alternatives?
Can the foresight bonus be made relative and stable beyond the tested length without introducing cache-score oscillations?
Which serving-path component causes per-turn latency to grow despite a fixed resident set?
How does PACE perform under many concurrent persistent sessions, tier pressure, and frequent remote restoration?
Can original temporal-distance information be retained explicitly for tasks where elapsed time or spacing is semantically meaningful?

problem.importance: Long-running agents can accumulate histories whose full KV state exceeds accelerator memory. If residency alone does not ensure usable context, eviction evaluations and agent-serving designs can appear successful while late-step correctness still deteriorates.
problem.scope: The work targets planned agent workloads in which future dependencies can be stated. It does not claim to provide an unrestricted long-context window or reliable recall of arbitrary, unplanned historical details.
problem.statement: Budgeted KV-cache systems optimize whether future-needed tokens remain resident, but the paper tests whether near-perfect residency is sufficient when retained tokens remain far from the query in rotary-position space.

proposed_experiments.baseline: Retention-only using the same planner, cache budget, persistent-session implementation, model, tasks, and generated trajectories; include H2O as a secondary reference.
proposed_experiments.hypothesis: PACE retains a statistically meaningful advantage over retention-only on natural planned-agent workloads when dependencies come from an imperfect production planner.
proposed_experiments.primary_metric: Paired end-to-end task success, stratified by planner edge precision and recall, with needed-span residency and rotary gap recorded at every dependent step.
proposed_experiments.stop_condition: Stop and reject the hypothesis if the pre-registered confidence interval for PACE minus retention-only includes zero or if benefit disappears in a majority of workload families.

proposed_experiments.baseline: The same retained-token set with positions as written, plus a full-context control where hardware permits.
proposed_experiments.hypothesis: Bounded renumbering does not degrade tasks whose answers depend on original temporal or positional distances.
proposed_experiments.primary_metric: Accuracy on pre-registered temporal-order, elapsed-distance, recency, and timestamp-grounded queries, reported alongside ordinary recall and likelihood.
proposed_experiments.stop_condition: Stop deployment-oriented validation if bounded positions produce a statistically significant accuracy loss or exceed a pre-declared non-inferiority margin on any safety-critical temporal category.

proposed_experiments.baseline: H2O, retention-only, and a retrieval-driven bounded-cache system under matched models, budgets, session traces, concurrency, and hardware.
proposed_experiments.hypothesis: PACE’s bounded KV state translates into useful production throughput under concurrency despite long-session latency growth and tier restoration.
proposed_experiments.primary_metric: Completed agent steps per second at fixed quality, with p50/p95/p99 latency, GPU and host memory, restoration frequency, and remote-tier bytes measured.
proposed_experiments.stop_condition: Stop if PACE fails to improve quality-adjusted throughput or violates pre-declared tail-latency and memory limits at any target concurrency level.

artifacts: The complete session templates and sampled-value ranges are included in the supplied document.

The paper specifies model versions, GPU and host memory, cache budget, engine path, decoding mode, position limits, statistical tests, seeds per configuration, integrity checks, and several pre-registration boundaries.
The implementation is stated to be a configuration-controlled subclass in an open-source inference engine.
Result files are stated to fingerprint instruction templates, and merge tooling rejects incompatible runs.
reproducibility.assessment: The procedural description is unusually detailed and includes templates, controls, integrity safeguards, factorial ablations, pre-registration statements, and hardware. However, the supplied material does not itself expose the implementation or raw artifacts needed to independently reproduce reported tables, so reproducibility is partial rather than strong.
missing: No repository snapshot, commit identifier, installation instructions, environment lockfile, runnable benchmark package, raw result files, pre-registration records, or exact reproduction commands are supplied in the document blocks.
The paper does not provide a matched full-cache 100K-token Qwen3-8B run.
Exact concurrent-serving and production-throughput reproduction procedures are absent.

results.context: Ten fresh 100K-token sessions, three probes per session, with a 2,048-token KV budget. This is the strongest controlled factorial comparison, although the 8K position limit had first been selected from an earlier distance sweep and was then tested on fresh seeds.

evidence.quote: Qwen3-8B, 100K-token sessions, B=2,048, ten fresh sessions, three probes each

results.result: In the pre-registered Qwen3-8B headline comparison, PACE passed 145/150 hidden checks (97%) and 28/30 probes completely, versus H2O at 63/150 (42%) and 7/30. Each single-component arm reached 94/150 (63%), while PACE recalled 100% of session facts.

results.context: Five 100K-token sessions per distance used the same seeds while moving only the definitions. This is stronger than the pooled distance analysis because session length is fixed, though only five sessions were used per point.

evidence.quote: five sessions per D, same seeds at every D
Residency is 0.992​–​0.996 for every PACE-family arm at every D.

results.result: The distance intervention supports the proposed mechanism: retention-only accuracy declined from 93% at a 2K logical gap to 64% at 90K despite residency of 0.992–0.996, whereas PACE with an 8K bound scored 97–100% and kept observed rotary gaps between 2.7K and 6.5K.

results.context: Five fresh Qwen3-8B sessions at each length placed definitions roughly 90% of the session before probes. These evaluations were pre-registered, but compare only bounded-position arms at the longest lengths and remain within the same synthetic task family.

results.result: The resident state remained bounded while execution overhead was measurable: PACE used 0.30 GB for the 2,048-token KV budget plus at most 0.30 GB for reference keys, versus a 147 GB full cache at 1M, and took 1,047 s versus 963 s (+9%) over ten 100K-token sessions.

results.context: This negative result limits the claim that bounded positions improve test-pass accuracy across models. The authors attribute limited separation partly to Mistral’s coding ceiling, while recall provides a less ceiling-constrained signal.

results.result: Generalization to the second model was mixed but informative: Mistral’s no-eviction control passed 40% of checks; PACE stayed near that ceiling, but its pre-declared 90K comparison against retention-only was not significant (46% versus 36%, p=0.75).
